found_values.value: High side on both paths, the onboard and the external. The ESC pack's return joins the boards' grounds at one star point, because an ESC's signal has no reference unless the returns meet. A shunt in the return would sit in parallel with the ESC's signal-ground path through the IO board, and part of the motor current would bypass it. The pack switches are high-side (V54 answer; the R3 row's external module 'is a high-side switch'). The sense leads therefore sit at up to 67.2 V to ground. Applied as 'common-mode' of the External shunt sense input and the Motor monitor
found_values.source: checkout e13f5f6: testbench/WIRING.md:37-47; hardware/docs/Research.md:614 (V54 Answer), :281; INA238 SLYS025B Table 4-1 (IN+ to the supply side for high-side), read 2026-09-29T09:45:51Z

found_values.value: From the external shunt's pack-side (IN+) sense lead; no separate lead. The voltage is measured at the pack, and on the high-side shunt (V177) that terminal is the pack voltage less the lead drop between pack and shunt. VBUS is a separate INA238 pin with 0.8 to 1.2 Mohm input impedance: 56 to 84 uA at 67.2 V. It is tapped ahead of the IN+ filter resistor, so that current does not flow through the resistor and add a shunt-voltage error. Applied as 'bus-voltage connection' of the External shunt sense input
found_values.source: checkout e13f5f6: docs/Screens.md:131-134; hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:428, :470; INA238 SLYS025B Table 4-1 pin 8 and section 5.5 (ZVBUS), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina238.pdf, read 2026-09-29T09:45:51Z

A lead on the wrong terminal, or the load side shorted with the switch closed, puts the whole pack (67.2 V, F15) across the leads. R3 holds the pack node under the 85 V absolute maximum of the parts on it, and the leads can see the same node up to that level. Applied as 'input withstand' of the External shunt sense input
